questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following reactions and facts of $\text{D}$-glucose cannot be explained by its open chain structure?

(i) Despite having the aldehyde group, glucose does not give Schiff test and $\text{2,4-DNP}$ test.

(ii) Glucose does not react with sodium hydrogen sulphite to form addition product.

(iii) The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with hydroxyl amine showing the absence of free-$\text{CHO}$ group.
questions.solution: The above behaviour could not be explained by the open chain structure. Because one of the –OH groups of glucose add to the –CHO group and form a cyclic hemiacetal structure. It was found that glucose forms a six membered ring in which –OH at C-5 is involved in ring formation. This explains the absence of –CHO group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If number of aldose, ketose, furanose and pyranose units present in maltose are p, q, r, s respectively. Find the value of $p + q + r + s$
questions.solution:
Monomer of maltose is $\alpha$ -D-glucopyranose. It is disaciharide, so 2 aldose and 2 pyranose forms are present in maltose.
Hence, p = 2, q = 0, r = 0 and s = 2
So, sum of p + q + r + s = 2 + 0 + 0 + 2 = 4.
